title: Whose Preferences? Differences in Fairness Preferences and Their Impact on the Fairness of AI Utilizing Human Feedback

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating content moderation fairness by modifying gender identifiers in text pairs (counterfactual substitution) and analyzing variations in fairness judgments between male and female annotators.

Modifying racial identifiers in comment pairs to evaluate individual fairness constraints and measuring differences in moderation preferences and downstream model predictions between White and Non-White annotators.
Comparing human fairness judgments on pairs of toxic online comments that differ only by religious group identifiers to see if they are treated equally.
Analyzing varying content moderation preferences based on the LGBTQ+ identity of annotators and evaluating sentences with sexual orientation identifiers in mixed-attribute sentence pairs.
Using logistic regression to analyze differences in content moderation fairness judgments across different annotator age demographics (e.g., under 38 vs. 38 and older).
Measuring variations in fairness judgments and downstream classifier performance for content moderation among annotators with different political stances (Democrat, Republican, Independent).

Evaluating how the educational level of annotators (e.g., No High School, High School, Bachelor's) influences their fairness preferences and predictions of the 'average American' judgment in content moderation.
